Good to know.

Can I use it as my everyday app?

Not yet. Alpha builds include sharing and optional control on Windows, Linux and Android, plus experimental Linux Wayland extension. Development builds add full-screen viewing, nearby-device discovery, network selection and an existing-screen picker with optional control on Windows. Android rotation and repeated sharing have emulator coverage; Android 10/11/14/16 emulator checks pass for taps, dragging, typing and control cleanup. Physical devices, long sessions, Windows virtual displays and production releases still need work.

Will it work over Wi-Fi?

That’s the primary goal. The current transport supports local networking, but real Wi-Fi playback, recovery and capture-to-display latency still need physical-device testing.

What about a USB-C cable?

Compatible Thunderbolt or USB4 networking can connect two computers directly. An arbitrary USB-C cable and two USB-C ports do not guarantee support. Ethernet is another wired option. Development builds include read-only network selection; it does not configure adapters. Capture and video processing still introduce delay.

Does my screen go to the cloud?

The app is designed to send screen data over your local network without a cloud account. Private session links and pinned TLS 1.3 protect implemented screen-sharing sessions. Opt-in nearby-device discovery has passed Android emulator checks. Private links remain required; stored device pairing is still planned.
